speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for seeing me. To help with your progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger, where exactly is the pain located, and does it involve the entire finger or just a specific joint?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detail; the mechanism of injury suggests a traumatic event. Did you hear or feel a loud "pop" or "snap" at the moment of injury, and is there any visible deformity or bruising on the finger now?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The inability to flex the distal interphalangeal joint and the finger resting in extension are classic signs of an injury to the extensor mechanism. Can you extend your middle finger while I observe if your ring finger extends with it, or does it stay flexed? Also, have you noticed a visible step-off or gap at the back of the distal interphalangeal joint?

REQUEST IMAGES: Right hand X-ray (AP and Lateral views) to rule out avulsion fracture.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Extensor Mavulsion Injury of the Distal Interphalangeal Joint.

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
